D007_l001.question:
A 51-year-old married male postman presents with a 1 year and 8 month history of mood and psychotic symptoms associated with significant functional decline. For approximately 1 year and 4 months, he has exhibited fixed false beliefs of serious bodily disease despite normal medical evaluations, along with marked withdrawal from social interactions and reduced engagement in previously routine interpersonal activities. 

Over the past 1 year and 2 months, he has experienced a persistent depressive episode characterized by frequent crying spells, notable unintentional weight loss (>5% within 1 month), psychomotor restlessness with difficulty remaining still, pronounced feelings of worthlessness, and subjective cognitive slowing with difficulty thinking clearly. He reports recurrent thoughts of death and self-harm without a formulated plan. These mood symptoms have interfered with occupational functioning and family roles.

Throughout the illness, somatic delusional beliefs have been prominent, accompanied by episodes of abnormal taste perceptions in the absence of stimuli. There has been at least a 2-week interval of persisting somatic delusions and gustatory hallucinations in the absence of significant depressive symptoms, though the depressive features have been present for the majority of the overall course.
D007_l001.options:
A. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    B. Bipolar I Disorder
    C. Schizoaffective Disorder (Depressive Type)
    D. Major Depressive Disorder with Psychotic Features
